newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher with bonds after data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher with bonds after data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were called higher on Thursday after September housing starts came in weaker than expected and weekly jobless claims pointed to an unexpectedly softer labour market, boosting bonds.

"Bonds are rallying on this. The housing starts weakness is more pronounced than the jobless claims. Both are friendly to bonds and stocks follow bonds," said Larry Wachtel, a market analyst at Prudential Securities.
The long bond, barely higher before the data, rose 13/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
Construction starts on new homes and apartments in September posted their biggest drop in 21 months, falling to the lowest level since last December, the U.S. Commerce Department said.
Housing starts fell six percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.438 million. That was below Wall Street economist forecasts for a 1.47-million-unit building rate.
